A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampling and molecular-simulation results for Müller–Brown, alanine dipeptide and transferable dipeptide models in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds protein experiments, model-capacity controls, six-bead alanine comparisons and structural and kinetic analyses.

M1.justification: The conservative graph transformer, denoising objective with weak Fokker–Planck regularization, finite-difference approximation and time-partitioned experts are retained. The simplified expert-selection equation describes the same procedure, and Ours denotes the existing Both model. Added applications and experimental configurations do not establish a revised core algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds Chignolin and BBA, a six-bead alanine benchmark using explicit-solvent reference trajectories, and restrained umbrella-sampling experiments. These substantially extend system size and evaluation conditions. Müller–Brown and earlier dipeptide coverage remain; moving AC and promoting KS does not constitute new coverage.

E2.justification: Table 13 introduces comparisons with Force Matching, Noise and Force Matching and Operator Forces, using published baseline results against models retrained on the corresponding six-bead system. Appendix C.2 also adds Wide and Deep capacity controls. The previous Diffusion, Two For One and Transferable BG comparators remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include protein training on 80% of reference samples, TICA-based evaluation with 100-bin histograms, the 100k-sample six-bead comparison, capacity controls and transition-state analyses. For existing alanine experiments, Both's reported regularization strength changes from 10^-4 to 10^-3 (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 3), without establishing whether this reflects rerunning or correcting the description.

E4.justification: v2 adds an ablation separating expert specialization from parameter count, protein component ablations, contact-map and nonlocal-distance analyses, and trajectory and transition-matrix diagnostics. Appendix C.7 also reports umbrella-sampling failures in poorly represented high-energy regions. These investigate substantial additional questions beyond the retained conservative-model, residual and bond analyses.

E5.justification: The existing three-training-seed alanine evaluation, ten-model toy evaluation and variation across test dipeptides are retained. Appendix B.4 introduces protein uncertainty estimates from three inference seeds using the same trained models, distinguishing inference variability from training variability. No increase in existing training repetitions or new significance-testing procedure is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial protein, force-matching, capacity and kinetic results. Existing results also change: alanine Both simulation PMF changes from 0.099±0.003 to 0.091±0.004 alongside the revised regularization setting; transferable Both simulation PMF changes from 0.183±0.070 to 0.203±0.104. These are revised results, not a uniform same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds an explicit flow-matching score relation, and B.1 supplies a discrete Langevin update. The original weak-residual derivation and coarse-graining formalism remain; removing the theorem box does not remove the result. The newly written update in Equation 33 has a positive potential-gradient term inconsistent with Equation 5's force convention.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution now explicitly claim accurate sampling and simulation of fast-folding proteins, whereas v1 left protein applications to future work. The efficiency contribution is also qualified: v1 promises no sacrifice in sampling performance, while v2 says efficiency gains can preserve high sampling quality. The central consistency and transferable-dipeptide contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges increased capacity as part of MoE's benefit, revises the earlier favorable interpretation of alanine iid performance, and develops protein fidelity-versus-consistency tradeoffs. It adds a concrete applicability boundary through umbrella-sampling failures. New kinetic interpretations are partly inconsistent: C.6.4 says MoE worsens transitions, but Chignolin Table 16 shows Both outperforming Fokker–Planck alone.

D1.justification: v2 adds learning-rate bounds, the identities of the fifteen evaluated dipeptides, detailed protein configurations, expanded hardware and runtime information, and a Langevin-update description. It also reports availability of model weights and self-contained JAX and PyTorch notebooks beyond v1's code announcement. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to every underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v2 extends positioning through discussions of Jamun and Target Score Matching, plus appendix connections to NETS/Hutchinson estimation, flow matching and Operator Forces. The primary distinctions from Two For One and FP-Diffusion remain. Publication updates for existing references, including Charron and Lewis, are not additional works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method motivation are extensively rewritten around agreement between denoising distributions and learned energies. The experimental narrative now leads with alanine and proteins, while the toy study and detailed alanine discussion move into a substantially reorganized appendix. This exceeds editing associated solely with added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 creates a combined alanine/protein comparison figure and summary table, adds structural, trajectory and transition displays, and relocates existing toy and alanine figures. Main-table JS columns remain available in appendix tables rather than being deleted. Existing line plots are restyled, and the main dipeptide illustration changes from AC to KS while retaining AC elsewhere.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evidential gaps in v1 through protein-scale validation, controls for the MoE capacity confound and comparisons with force-matching methods. Structural and kinetic diagnostics, explicit umbrella-sampling failures and expanded reproducibility information substantially strengthen assessment of the central claims. These gains outweigh local reporting errors, including Equation 33's inconsistency with Equation 5 and the kinetic interpretation contradicted by Chignolin Table 16.
